rationale: Prior-day high, low and close and the session VWAP are where resting orders sit, so a 5-minute bar that pokes to one and is rejected with a long wick shows those orders absorbed the push, and price reverses; the main setting is how long the wick must be. Losing side: Breakout traders who buy or sell the poke into the prior-day level and are trapped when it is rejected.
notes: C / R#13: tf bar with wick >= `wick` of its range and its extreme within 0.25 ATR of a key level (prior-day H/L/C, overnight H/L in NY sessions, session VWAP) -> reversal at market; struct = wick end
